name: Blackish Violet
lede: Blackish Violet is a dark, smoky indigo-purple, [[violet|Violet]] pushed almost to black by the modifier "blackish," one of the long compound-name families Robert Ridgway built for his 1912 color nomenclature.

sections.title: A modifier on a named hue
sections.body:
The name follows the grammar "blackish" plus the parent hue [[violet|Violet]]: the modifier marks a darkened, desaturated version of that base color, not a separate pigment or dye [1]. Robert Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* (1912) first records a close match, at plate X, hue 59, tone m [1]. The ISCC-NBS system picked it up again in 1955, filing it in block 211 under the violet family [1].

Measured, the swatch reads as a grayish violet by ISCC-NBS terms, about 4.8 units from the historical plate color, with Munsell notation 0.7P 2.8/5.2 [1]. The closest look-alikes in our data are [[plum-purple|Plum Purple]], 2.6 units away, [[toga|Toga]], almost the same shade, and [[corsican-blue|Corsican Blue]], more vivid [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, finds this dark violet in 22 of them, about 0.09 percent, rarer than 66 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1800s, at 1.4 times the expected rate for that century (7 of 8,345 paintings from then), and inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, 50 percent of the time, by lightness rank rather than raw area [2].

The earliest match in our archive is dated 1340, by Pietro Lorenzetti, 572 years before Ridgway's 1912 record [2]. Our archive's early centuries are thin, so that date is a floor, not a first, and the match is only a look-alike hue, not proof a matching dye or pigment existed then [2].
